# The ingenuity and creativity of EAFIT students is concentrated in Inventiva

**Until this Friday, May 31, hundreds of projects developed by students from the different undergraduate programs of the School of Applied Sciences and Engineering, and the undergraduate program of Interactive Design at EAFIT are presented to the community at the Inventiva Fair.**

**This event is led by different departments of the University and is held within the framework of the third edition of Acción EAFIT, a week dedicated to experiential learning through various training activities, exhibitions and displays.**

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [News](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias)
- [Our Impact](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias/nuestro-impacto)
- The Ingenuity and Creativity of EAFIT Students Focuses on Inventiveness

![Imagen El ingenio y la creatividad de los estudiantes de EAFIT se concentra en Inventiva](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/eddf4739-a1e8-4377-ab55-2a8840c1cb4d/web/Agencoa-31-mayo.jpg?crop=yes&k=c&w=823&h=450&itok=uoDmfSKI)

The Inventiva projects are on display in the Student Plaza between 9:00 am and 6:00 pm until this Friday, May 31st.

A roaring engine interrupts conversations and draws curious onlookers to the source of the sound. The _buggies_ —lightweight vehicles—have arrived, designed and presented by graduating Mechanical Engineering students from EAFIT University. This exhibition, promoted by the Vice-Rectorate for Learning and the University's Student Organization, showcases projects developed by students from various undergraduate programs within the School of Applied Sciences and Engineering, as well as the Interactive Design program, until Friday, May 31, from 9:00 am to 6:00 pm in the Student Plaza.

This fair takes place within the framework of the third edition of Acción EAFIT, a week where the university community has shared different challenges and solutions in various areas, connecting the talent of students with proposals that bring to life the educational model of the University, with its focus on experiential learning.

Manuela Mejía Hurtado, a fifth-semester Administration student and one of the organizers of the exhibition, states that “Inventiva seeks to give students the opportunity to present and share their projects, to demonstrate experiential learning, and the development of innovative ideas and products, which have been supported by professors throughout the semester.”

During 18 weeks of work, adds Laura Galvis, a third-semester student of Urban Design and Habitat Management and also an organizer of the exhibition, the students dedicated a large part of their time to trial and error in the University's workshops, which is why she considers it valuable to share all these skills with the university community. She also recalls the beginnings of the event and their vision for the future.

“At one point it was called Expo Ingenierías, but then it was changed to Inventiva because it grew much more and now includes other programs. For the future, we hope it will be a city event, so that people from outside can learn about what EAFIT students and future graduates can achieve,” says Laura.

### Solving challenges and learning how to do it.

Anthony Giraldo Posada and his first-semester Mechanical Engineering classmates faced the challenge of building a boat for their School Project course. The process involved several stages, including creating a _mood board_ , conducting interviews, and selecting a sustainable material. His group chose to use MDF and recycle pine from the woodworking lab. “The development of this boat was free-flowing, so we had a lot of trial and error, and that's how we learned different things. I, for example, had never worked with wood before; now I know more about how it works,” he says.

For their part, María José Valencia and Juanita Urrea, eighth-semester Production Engineering students, developed a router for their Machine and Equipment Elements Project course. This machine allows for the marking of any type of design on a surface, using software as part of the process. “Having these kinds of spaces is valuable not only for university students, but also for those in high school who don't know what to study. It's good to be able to show them what we do so they can learn about different career paths,” says María José.

Mechanical Engineering students enthusiastically presented their projects. Samuel Gómez, a fifth-semester student, worked with his classmates on a Human-Powered Vehicle (HPV), which is propelled by a person's strength and used for racing, mountain climbing, and even getting around town. "I feel that you learn much more this way than just studying the topic and watching videos or learning formulas. I think that doing it experimentally leads to a better understanding," he said about the project.

En la materia de Diseño de Máquinas, Jordan Yesid Morales Nieves y Juan José Ramírez Palacio, estudiantes de noveno semestre de Ingeniería Mecánica, construyeron un _buggy_ con motor a combustión, refrigerado por agua, con encendido eléctrico y freno de disco. “Realmente no es como en el papel, sino que uno se encuentra con muchos tropiezos que tiene que solucionar en el momento”, dice Jordan Yesid. Algo en lo que coincide Juan José, quien añade: “Tener la experiencia y saber cómo reaccionar ante posibles problemas es muy valioso en la industria”.

El sábado 1 de junio, a las 10:00 a.m., en el Coliseo Guayabos, se realizará la premiación de los proyectos ganadores de Inventiva. Durante cada jornada de la muestra, los visitantes de la feria tienen la posibilidad de votar por el proyecto que más les ha gustado.

metadata.ogTitle: El ingenio y la creatividad de los estudiantes de EAFIT se concentra en Inventiva
metadata.ogDescription: ​Un motor que se enciende a todo volumen interrumpe las conversaciones e invita a las miradas curiosas a encontrar la fuente del sonido. Llegaron los buggys —vehículos de chasis ligero— que los estudiantes de último semestre de Ingeniería Mecánica de EAFIT elaboraron y presentaron en Inventiva, la muestra promovida por la Vicerrectoría de Aprendizaje y la Organización Estudiantil de la Universidad, en la que se exponen, hasta este viernes 31 de mayo, de 9:00 a.m. a 6:00 p.m.
